key_insight: Turbulence alters ice-crystal alignment and scattering, causing ice-water-content retrievals that assume perfect horizontal alignment to underestimate content in the Rayleigh regime.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for orientation statistics can reduce bias in radar, lidar and submillimeter ice-cloud retrievals.
method: Model spheroid orientations using settling-induced torque, turbulent gradients, rotational diffusion and intermittency.
Average Rayleigh, Rayleigh–Gans, T-matrix and specular scattering over orientation distributions.
Express turbulence effects through Legendre moments and assess retrieval biases.
evidence_signal: For single-size populations of the studied shapes, combining specific differential phase and differential reflectivity limits retrieval bias to 25%; exploratory EarthCARE lidar analysis finds a compatible signature most frequent near −11 °C.
watch_item: The 25% bias bound can fail for size distributions spanning the alignment transition because the two observables weight crystal sizes differently.
paper_title: Scattering by Small Ice Crystals in Turbulence: From Orientation Statistics to Retrieval Biases
